explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/197: ℕ can be split into complementary sets A and B, each admitting an enumeration (ℕ ≃ A, ℕ ≃ B) with no monotone 3-term AP. Using bijections with ℕ forces both parts to be infinite. That is the meaningful case, since a finite part would leave a cofinite part to which the DEGS argument applies. The open question is stated affirmatively.
